A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProbHardE2E work. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–I support reliable comparison, including matching content relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original PDE and hierarchical forecasting experiments, including accuracy, constraint errors, uncertainty estimates, and computational timings in Section 4 and Appendix I.

after.justification: V2 retains original PDE and hierarchical forecasting results, including the nonlinear conservation and total-variation case studies.

M1.justification: The DPPL, projection procedures, backbones, and CRPS objective are retained. V2 explicitly separates parameter projection during training from sample projection at inference, but both procedures were already described in v1 Section 3.2 and Appendix C.4. The rewritten Algorithm 1 does not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Heat, PME, Stefan, and linear advection, alongside Labour, Tourism, Tourism-L, Traffic, and Wiki. The nonlinear-PME parameter ranges and TVD scenario are also retained in Appendix I.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding linear-PDE, nonlinear-PME, and forecasting comparisons: v1 Tables 1–3 become v2 Tables 2–4. ProbHardInf was already evaluated in v1; the added references do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix H.3 explicitly evaluates PDE constraint error on predicted means; v2 specifies evaluation over 100 predictive samples. This materially changes the central feasibility test, especially for nonlinear constraints. Other splits, training settings, and accuracy metrics are retained. The PDFs do not establish reruns, and v2's equation shows a sum although its prose specifies an average.

E4.justification: The projection-type comparisons, CRPS-versus-NLL comparisons, sampling-cost analyses, nonlinear-PME studies, and TVD/shock illustrations are retained. Section 4 and Appendix I introduce no additional ablation, robustness test, or case study.

E5.justification: Both versions report five forecasting evaluations with CRPS means and variances in Appendix H.2.3, and retain the same uncertainty reporting and predictive bands. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice changes. The 100 predictive draws concern the revised CE evaluation, not additional independent runs.

E6.justification: Numerical table entries and plotted results are retained, apart from equivalent rounding. However, v2 Section 4.2.1 newly reports the nonlinear-PME zero CE values as demonstrating feasibility of samples, whereas v1 Appendix H.3 attributed PDE CE to means. This is a revised reported finding under a changed evaluation definition, not a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds an assertion that the linearization error converges to zero in probability, citing Van der Vaart. The theorem statements and existing projection and approximation derivations remain. Appendix H.3 also replaces the single-output CE expression with aggregation over samples.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a general probabilistic DPPL framework, hard constraints, uncertainty quantification, and efficient CRPS training. The headline accuracy and training-speed claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the nonlinear results as validating approximate parameter projection during training combined with exact sample projection at inference. It also adds extension beyond location-scale distributions as future work. The underlying approximation limitation and sample-projection remedy were already discussed in v1 Appendix C.4.

D1.justification: Section 3.4.2 newly identifies the nonlinear inference solver as custom and batched. Existing CVXPYLayers information, hardware, architectures, and hyperparameter tables are retained; no new code or data release is documented.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Utkarsh et al. (2025), Hyndman et al. (2025), Olivares et al. (2022), and Van der Vaart (2000), and removes Lakshminarayanan et al. (2017). The broader positioning and Appendix A survey remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites tighten the abstract and introduction and emphasize training versus inference in Algorithm 1 and Sections 3.2–3.4. Duplicated main-text propositions are retained in Appendix C, and the former C.4 explanation is incorporated into the main narrative. The overall section sequence and most appendix prose remain.

P2.justification: V1's appendix Table 5 becomes v2's main-text Table 1 with a shorter caption. Existing result tables are renumbered, and figures and tables are repositioned through the document. All five figures retain the same graphical content; no new visualization is added.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the training/inference distinction clearer in Algorithm 1 and Sections 3.2–3.4. However, it presents unchanged CE entries as evidence about samples instead of means, while Appendix H.3 inconsistently defines their aggregation as both a sum and an average. The PDFs do not reconcile this central validation claim, so the clarity gains cannot be weighed reliably against the new reporting ambiguity.
